desk_read: The dominant theme yesterday was a sharp risk-off move in equities alongside a strong bid in energy, with crude leading the charge. Brent outperformed WTI, gaining +3.72% on above-average volume of 1.2x, while WTI added +2.61% on average turnover; both curves remain in backwardation, though the spreads eased modestly on the session. Equity selling was heaviest in the Nasdaq 100, off -2.50% on 1.4x average volume, with the forward spread widening sharply, suggesting the selloff carried real weight. Natural gas diverged from the energy rally, falling -3.71% while total open interest edged up +2.1k contracts, a flow read of new shorts entering into weakness — the one market where positioning and price are moving in the same bearish direction.
oil_read: Oil Desk — WTI & Brent Both markets rallied hard — WTI +2.61% and Brent +3.72% — on volume of 1.0x and 1.2x their respective 20-day averages, suggesting the move was reasonably well-participated rather than thin-market noise. Net open interest changes were flat for both, so the price gains reflect repricing of existing positions rather than a clear influx of new length. Both curves remain in backwardation, with WTI's CLX26–CLJ27 spread at +9.04 $/bbl and Brent's BZZ26–BZK27 at +12.09 $/bbl, though both spreads eased versus the prior session.
